title: Japan Is Getting Its First Disney Cruise Ship
paragraphs: Disney fans in Japan already have two theme parks where they can visit "the happiest place on Earth." Soon, they'll have another Disney destination — this time on the water.
Japan's first Disney cruise ship has officially been named Disney Imagination, and it's set to begin sailing from Tokyo in spring 2029.

The ship will be operated by Oriental Land, the company behind Tokyo Disneyland and Tokyo DisneySea, and will offer mostly short cruises of two to four nights. Prices for standard rooms will start at around 100,000 yen per person, or about $630.
At around 340 meters long, Disney Imagination will have 1,250 guest rooms and space for about 4,000 passengers.
And, of course, there will be lots of Disney magic on board!
Guests will be able to watch stage shows in a theater with more than 1,300 seats, see character shows on an outdoor deck and meet Disney characters dressed in special cruise outfits.
There will be three main themed restaurants and around 30 other places to eat and drink, as well as special areas just for children.

The outside of the ship will also get a Disney touch. On the back, there will be a picture of Ariel from The Little Mermaid, along with Sebastian and other friends from under the sea. Ariel will be shown writing the ship's name with her famous "dinglehopper" — or what most of us would call a "fork."
Disney has been taking its magic to sea for nearly three decades now. Its first cruise ship, Disney Magic, began sailing in 1998.
Today, Disney Cruise Line has eight ships. Its newest, Disney Adventure, began sailing from Singapore in March 2026, and five more are planned by 2031 — including Disney Imagination in Japan.
